action: Chapter title card and agenda slides list body, hands and feet forms.
why: Frames the chapter: forms first, then hands, then feet.

action: Slide states that observing the reference matters more than memorised anatomy.
why: Sets the method: copy what the reference shows.

action: Second slide paragraph adds that anatomy charts are not required, only translating reference to 3D.
why: Reinforces reference-driven sculpting.

action: Same slide held while narrator repeats that muscles need not be memorised.
why: Method statement, no Blender action.

action: Slide adds that the reference becomes the anatomy guide, then a new heading 'The arms' appears.
why: Reference choice drives proportions and volumes.

action: Legs slide: photo of a side-view leg and an anatomy drawing appear beside the straight-versus-curves text.
why: Illustrates front-curved thigh, back-curved calf.

action: Red strokes are drawn over the side-view leg photo marking curved front of thigh, straight back, and the opposite on the calf.
why: Shows the alternating curve rhythm to copy.

action: Angry-face diagram added: eyebrow lines slope down toward the middle of the lower leg, with ankle-bone diagram.
why: Outer calf bulge sits higher than the inner one.

action: Narrator points at the angry-face diagram and ankle diagram; inner ankle higher than outer.
why: Ankle height rule.

action: Same collage, cursor dots on ankle diagram showing correct tilt versus a flat horizontal line.
why: Ankle height rule repeated.

action: A red line is drawn across the wrong ankle diagram (level) and a tilted red line across the right one; then a Torso slide starts.
why: Contrast: never level ankles.

action: Torso slide shows a front and back grey anatomy sculpt; text says torso depends heavily on reference and should flow with balance.
view: front and back anatomy sculpt images
why: Torso varies by character type; use reference.

action: Narrator calls the anatomy sculpt a nice example of rhythm and balance even in a stiff pose.
view: front and back anatomy sculpt images
why: Even an A-pose body needs rhythm.

action: Switches to the reference board app and shows a hands study sheet; a red box is drawn on the palm of a hand photo.
why: Palm is a rectangle plus a thumb wedge.

action: Slide text: palm is a rectangle with a wedge for the thumb; then 'the palm is not flat' paragraph appears.
why: Simple shapes first, with natural palm curvature.

action: Back on slides, then the board: a hand photo with red palm outline; text says knuckles sit on a curve.
why: Palm curved, knuckles on an arc.

action: Red arcs drawn across a hand sculpt photo through each row of knuckles; each arc is steeper than the one before.
why: Show finger-joint rows follow progressively steeper arcs.

action: Red ticks drawn over a side-view finger photo: knuckle to tip is one unit, first joint at half, second joint at half again.
why: Finger proportion rule, then slide with joint-angle text.

action: Red and green boxes compare a straight finger (bad) with an arched, three-angle finger (good); then slides switch to feet.
why: Avoid straight-tube fingers; use three angled segments.

action: Feet slide shows front/side triangle drawings, a bottom-view rectangle with sides pushed in, and a side arch note.
why: Foot as triangle from front and side, rectangle from below.

action: Stepped-toes paragraph appears beside a green foot sculpt showing toes stepping down; cursor marks along the toe tops.
why: Toes step down instead of sitting level.

action: Blender opens in the Sculpting workspace on the stage 03 head and torso, with the reference board docked on the left; view zooms out from face to chest.
view: front, zooming out from the face
why: Starting state of the body stage.

action: Narrator scrolls the reference board to the foot and hand references, then zooms out to the full figure in front, then a three-quarter view.
why: Show gathered hand and foot references, check whole figure.

action: Adds a cube in Object Mode; it appears large over the head until scaled down to hand size beside the figure.
why: Start the hand with a simple box.

action: Moves cube to the forearm end, flattens it, then in Edit Mode adds a loop cut along the middle and raises it so the palm arches.
tool: Edit Mode, Loop Cut and Slide, G move
why: Palm must have curvature.
reader_equivalent: grab on back of palm along its normal

action: Adds a second and third loop cut and nudges them so the palm has a visible arch across the width; cube is narrowed toward the wrist.
why: More arch control and the start of the thumb wedge.

action: In Sculpt Mode the Grab brush (Strength 0.400, Radius about 284 px) tidies the hand block next to the arm; Ctrl+Tab then returns to Object Mode.
why: Soften and fit hand block to arm.

action: Edit Mode with Mirror modifier visible (axis X, merge 0.001 m); another loop cut is added at the wrist, then the modifier menu is searched for Subdivision Surface.
why: Prepare Mirror plus Subdivision preview for the palm.

action: Sculpt Mode Grab (Radius about 200 px, Strength 0.400) thins the soft Subdivision-smoothed palm; the Subdivision panel reads viewport 1, render 2.
why: Shape the palm block under Subdivision.

action: Edit Mode: pulls the thumb-side wedge of the palm down; Ctrl+Tab back to Object Mode with Mirror and Subdivision still on.
why: Indicate the fleshy part opposite the thumb; refine later after subdivision.

action: Adds a new cube near the face in Edit Mode, with Alt+Z x-ray; scale/extrude it into a long thin bar.
why: Start a finger as one extruded edge.

action: Object Mode, Add Modifier search: Skin first, then Subdivision Surface; Subdivision levels raised from 1 to 2 in the panel.
why: Skin gives round thickness; subdivision smooths it.

action: Edit Mode: scales the whole vertex set smaller with S, so the skin tube thins; panel shows Skin symmetry X on and Subdivision levels 2.
tool: Skin modifier, scale in Edit Mode
why: Set finger thickness; do not move the first vertex so the origin stays at the knuckle.

action: Object Mode: rotates the finger (R) in the object-level view, then Numpad 1 to front orthographic of the whole figure.
why: Origin at the knuckle lets the finger turn about its base.

action: Moves the finger (G) onto the palm's front edge as the index finger, with the hand shown from the side.
why: Place the first finger before duplicating.

action: Four straight fingers of near-equal length stand on the palm; Edit Mode with X-ray and Ctrl+R loop cut across the middle of the fingers.
why: Add a joint to refine finger shape.

action: Fingers adjusted into fan with differing lengths; the thumb is made next by reusing a finger copy.
why: Roughly right lengths and spread, refine later in sculpt.

action: Edit Mode: scales thumb and reshapes palm to meet it, then opens the Subdivision modifier dropdown to pick Apply on the palm.
why: Bake the palm smoothing so it can be sculpted.

action: Sculpt Mode Grab (Radius about 540 px, Strength 0.400) pulls forearm and palm area; then Ctrl+Tab and Shift+Esc; fingers selected in Object Mode.
view: perspective, zoomed from arm to figure
why: Make forearm end meet the wrist.

action: Sets pivot back to median point, selects the four fingers and tries to apply modifiers on them.
why: Prepare to bake modifiers on linked fingers.

action: An Apply Modifier warning dialog appears; instead Ctrl+A > Visual Geometry to Mesh is chosen and all four fingers lose their modifier stacks.
tool: Object > Apply > Visual Geometry to Mesh
why: Linked data cannot take a normal modifier apply.

action: Sculpt Mode on one finger with Grab (Radius about 324 px, Strength 0.400); the edit appears on all four linked fingers.
why: One sculpt edit changes every linked finger.

action: Rotates the thumb and fingers to follow palm curvature; Grab at Radius about 160 px, Strength 0.400 in Sculpt Mode.
why: Fit fingers to the arc of the palm.

action: Uses the Annotate tool to scribble joint marks, then Crease Polish (Radius about 84 then 68 px, Strength 0.250) draws a faint crease across the finger underside; annotation erased.
why: Mark the joints lightly.

action: Grab (Radius 162-216 px, Strength 0.400) rounds the fingertips from several angles; narrator skips nails for this character.
why: Shape the last segment before creases; no nails.

action: Grab at Radius about 250 px, Strength 0.400 on the thumb tip, undoing a couple of strokes with Ctrl+Z; checks whether symmetry helps the thumb.
why: The thumb usually does not mirror correctly; correct both sides by hand.

action: File saved as an incremental version; Grab (Radius about 304-366 px, Strength 0.400) smooths the forearm-to-palm transition from several angles.
why: Prepare the palm for more resolution.

action: Orbits to front orthographic with a large Grab ring (about 528 px); narrator isolates the hand with Alt+B clip region (viewport title says Clipped).
why: Hide nearby blockout parts without hiding them.

action: Hand viewed from the palm side with a palm-photo reference docked at the left; cursor hovers over the thumb pad in the reference.
why: Compare against reference; translate what is seen.

action: Scrape/Fill (Radius about 160-200 px, Strength 0.700, red ring) flattens the back of the palm with sweeping strokes; ring turns red.
why: Flatten the top of the palm.

action: Continues Scrape/Fill on palm top, then orbits around the forearm and hand to check the shape.
why: Check the palm shape from other sides.

action: Selects one finger in Object Mode, enters Sculpt Mode and drags the Voxel Remesh size: readout falls from 0.0998 m to 0.0114 m on the finger.
why: Add resolution to the fingers.

action: Clay Strips (Radius 112 then 286 px, Strength 0.500) adds volume on finger undersides; Shift held to smooth afterwards.
why: Build finger pads, then smooth.

action: Crease Polish (Radius 110-120 px, Strength 0.250) draws subtle creases at the two finger joints; Shift smooths them.
why: Keep joint creases faint.

action: Thumb voxel remesh readout 0.0106 m; then Grab (Radius 320-542 px) shapes the thumb and Shift smooths gently so forms survive.
why: Same 0.01 resolution as the fingers.

action: Hand zoomed out, orbit to check; narrator declares fingers done and ready to merge.
why: All parts are final before joining.

action: Object Mode: selects fingers and thumb, makes the palm active, joins with Ctrl+J (narrator says Ctrl G), then Sculpt Mode.
why: Make one mesh for the hand.
reader_equivalent: join_and_fuse([palm, thumb, f1, f2, f3, f4], palm, v)

action: Voxel size dragged down; readouts 0.0160, 0.0145, 0.0129, 0.0100 m shown over the hand as the preview grid gets finer.
why: Fuse at about 0.01 so fingers do not web.

action: Orbits the hand with Grab (Radius 86 px, Strength 0.400) idle; narrator warns each finger must now be sculpted separately and to Ctrl+Z if a finger needs changing.
why: Check fingers before the fuse remesh.

action: Presses Ctrl+R to fuse; the finger roots show ragged stair-steps where each finger meets the palm.
why: Merge the joined hand into one skin.

action: Clay Strips (Radius 60-176 px, Strength 0.500) builds up the web between finger roots on the back of the hand; Shift smooths.
why: Blend each finger root into the palm.

action: Smooths the palm, then Crease Polish (Radius 208-344 px then 80 px, Strength 0.250) draws palm lines copied from the reference.
why: Add palm lines from the reference.

action: Crease Polish (Radius 56-82 px, Strength 0.250) with Ctrl held marks each knuckle on the back of the hand.
why: Define knuckles.

action: Ctrl-creases the knuckles, then Scrape/Fill (Radius 144-274 px, Strength 0.700) flattens the sides of the hand and wrist.
why: Flat sides read as a real hand.

action: Another voxel remesh readout of 0.0100 m on the whole hand; narrator says finer remesh is possible but skipped.
why: Option to raise resolution further.

action: Crease Polish (Radius 52-70 px, Strength 0.250) adds small knuckle creases and a thumb crease; view orbits and zooms out to full body.
why: Final hand creases.

action: Hand finished; Alt+B clip toggled off and the view zooms out to the whole body to start on the feet.
why: Move on to feet.

action: A rounded cube lies beside the legs; Annotate pen scribbles, then bottom orthographic view via the viewport gizmo shows legs and a foot ellipse; Grab (Radius 284 px, Strength 0.400) starts shaping the rectangle from below.
why: Foot is a rectangle from below.

action: Grab (Radius 380 px, Strength 0.400) pulls the shape from the front and side; the rounded cube sits under the ankle.
why: Pull the foot block to the right length and width.

action: Ctrl+Z after a lasso mask covered only the near side; the Lasso Mask tool-header toggle 'Front Faces Only' is ticked and gets unticked.
why: Mask must pass through the block.

action: Grab (Radius 434 px, Strength 0.400) lifts the front into a triangle; Annotate pen draws guide lines on the foot in front view and is then erased.
why: Foot as a right-angled triangle, not an isosceles one.

action: Grab (Radius 266-438 px) adjusts the ankle block from several angles; Shift smooths the area so the junction is not sharp.
why: Soften the ankle transition.

action: Right orthographic (Numpad 3): foot is a flat wedge; Grab at Radius about 298-306 px; then reaches into the toolbar for the lasso-type tool.
why: Slice and shape sole from the side.

action: Annotate pen outlines the foot footprint from below and marks where the toes will start; then Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode.
why: Locate the toe shelf before adding toes.

action: Side view: adds a Skin plus Subdivision toe (levels 1 then 2), scales all with Ctrl+A to size, moves it to the front of the foot in Object Mode.
why: Toes built like fingers.

action: Rotates the big toe, then in Edit Mode shapes it stepped (loops slid, lowered) while a foot reference sits in the left panel.
why: Stepped top of big toe.

action: Alt+D duplicates the big toe, scale along its Y (length) axis in Object Mode to make the second toe shorter; moves it beside the first.
why: Linked toes shrink toward the outer edge.

action: Front orthographic: five toe balls lie in a row in front of the foot (big toe largest, others smaller); then selects the foot and enters Sculpt Mode with Grab (Radius about 420 px) to bring the block down.
why: Make the foot block meet the toes.

action: Toes shown from the front/top with a stepped profile, then selects all toes with Ctrl+click.
why: Group toes for baking.

action: Inflate/Deflate (Radius about 420 px, Strength 0.500) rounds the heel from behind; Grab (Radius 342-420 px) refines; heel reads as a teardrop; symmetry checked both sides.
why: Heel teardrop from behind.

action: Foot moves into place; remesh preview readouts show 0.0752 m then 0.0103 m on a toe; Grab (Radius 206 px) sculpts the toes.
why: Toes remeshed at about 0.01.

action: Scrape/Fill (Radius 276 px, Strength 0.700) flattens the top of the foot and toes; Shift smooths; then the foot is selected in Object Mode to join the toes.
why: Make toe-to-foot transitions clean before joining.

action: Joins toes with the foot using Ctrl+J, then Ctrl+R: preview readouts fall 0.0132 then 0.00642 m.
why: Fuse the foot at a very fine voxel.

action: Remesh done; Scrape/Fill (Radius 114 px, Strength 0.700) and Clay Strips (Radius 54 px, Strength 0.500) smooth and rebuild toe-to-foot transitions on top.
view: perspective, top of foot and toes
why: Blend toe roots into the foot.

action: Grab (Radius 180-304 px, Strength 0.400) pushes the pinky toe in, then Shift smooths the gaps; creases already drawn between toes show as thin lines.
why: Clean transitions toe by toe.

action: Grab and then Inflate/Deflate (Radius 344 px, Strength 0.500) adjusts toe tips; the artist keeps wide gaps between toes for later retopology.
why: Leave room between toes.

action: Returns to the body; selects the legs, Crease Polish tool active, remesh readout 0.0495 m on the leg; reference board now shows the body pages.
why: Start legs at about 0.05.

action: Hides other body parts (H x3), uses right orthographic, draws annotation lines along the thigh, then Grab (Radius 412 px, Strength 0.400) makes the front of the thigh curved.
why: Front curved, back straight.

action: Grab (Radius 264-358 px, Strength 0.400) sweeps the side of the thigh to curve it and defines the hip, in right orthographic and then perspective.
why: Thigh front curve, hip definition.

action: Zooms out to front and perspective to judge the upper leg; calls it done; then selects the lower legs (Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode) to add resolution.
why: Check the whole leg silhouette before the next part.

action: Lower leg: Grab (Radius 224 px) with Shift smoothing, Annotate lines drawn on the side view to mark the calf curve and knee; Alt+Q (move to cursor) and Ctrl strokes.
why: Make lower leg flow into the upper leg; calf back curved.

action: Pelvis: Ctrl+R remesh, then Grab (Radius 250-424 px, Strength 0.400) and Shift smoothing across the pelvis and buttock.
why: Rounded pelvis and seat.

action: Crease Polish (Radius 88-348 px, Strength 0.250) marks the gluteal split and fold toward the leg; Grab (Radius 410 px) rounds the seat so it does not intersect.
why: Gluteal split and leg fold.

action: Chest: side view shows the stage 02 chest; Crease Polish (Radius 80-410 px, Strength 0.250) draws the lower rib-cage edge arch, with a body reference docked at left.
why: Rib cage lower edge as an arch.

action: Clay Strips (Radius 312 px, Strength 0.500) builds up hips with Shift smoothing, then Grab (Radius 226 px) refines; zooms out to front to compare.
why: Hip shape from the reference.

action: Unhides all objects, deletes the stage 02 hand and foot placeholders, then File > Save Incremental.
why: Old placeholders no longer needed; new numbered save.

action: Deletion confirmation dialog, then selects both arms and enters Sculpt Mode; remesh preview reads 0.0526 m on the upper arm.
why: Arms get their own pass at about 0.05.

action: Ctrl-held Crease Polish (Radius 54-70 px, Strength 0.250) marks the elbow, then Scrape/Fill (Radius 114 px, Strength 0.700) flattens the top of the elbow point.
why: Mark elbow with a crease and flat plane.

action: Shoulder: Grab (Radius 244 px, Strength 0.400), Shift smooths; Ctrl+R remesh on the shoulder and neck at a coarse size to merge with neighbors.
why: Shoulder and neck only remeshed and smoothed.

action: Smooths the neck, then in Object Mode selects both leg parts and joins them with Ctrl+J.
why: Join upper and lower leg.

action: Saves with Ctrl+S, then remesh readout of 0.0405 m on the leg; Ctrl+R at about 0.04.
why: Fuse upper and lower leg.

action: Clay Strips (Radius 56-238 px, Strength 0.500) builds across the knee front, Shift smooths the ridges.
why: Blend the knee seam.

action: Crease Polish (Radius 100 px, Strength 0.250) above the kneecap; Grab (Radius 280-320 px, Strength 0.400) pulls the back of the knee out; Shift smooths.
view: close perspective, side of the knee
why: Faint knee creases; check straight versus curved.

action: Side view: Annotate marks the back line; Grab (Radius 310-442 px, Strength 0.400) pulls the lower back in so the back reads as an S; Alt+Q moves view to cursor.
why: S-curve of the lower back from the side.

action: Selects the three torso parts in Object Mode, joins them with Ctrl+J (narrator says Ctrl G), Sculpt Mode, Ctrl+R at about 0.03 and smooths.
why: Fuse chest, waist and pelvis.

action: Grab (Radius 124-314 px, Strength 0.400) from front and behind drags the buttocks down so they overlap the legs; Shift smooths the seams; hip line lifted.
why: Buttocks overlap the legs.

action: Clay Strips (Radius 218 px, Strength 0.500), then Crease Polish (Radius 114 px, Strength 0.250) marks the fold at the waist side, copied from the body reference docked left.
why: Side-of-waist crease from the reference.

action: Clay Strips (Radius 90-302 px, Strength 0.500) and Shift-smooth the side; Crease Polish (Radius 82 px, Strength 0.250) marks the vertical centre line of the belly.
why: Belly centre line from the reference.

action: Crease Polish (Radius 70-118 px, Strength 0.250) continues the centre line down; narrator stresses copying what the reference shows.
why: Observation, not memory.

action: Compares to the reference (cursor on it), then Crease Polish (Radius 60-70 px, Strength 0.250) drags a crease at the side of the stomach; a faint navel dimple already visible.
why: Define the stomach.

action: Clay Strips (Radius 76-344 px, Strength 0.500) adds volume low on the belly; Shift smooths everything; view zooms out.
why: Add belly volume and blend.

action: Grab (Radius 224-329 px, Strength 0.400) lowers the breasts, then Inflate/Deflate (Radius 270 px, Strength 0.500) fills them; front view with reference at left.
why: Chest volume and fullness.

action: Whole figure shown with the chest done; the artist selects both arms and goes to merge the hands into them; Ctrl+R for the remesh.
why: Next step: join arm parts.

action: Clay Strips (Radius 348 px, Strength 0.500) and Grab (Radius 470 px) refine the elbow, Inflate (Radius 504 px, Strength 0.500) fills the forearm; orbits all around.
view: close perspective, elbow, then whole figure
why: Blend elbow; check from all angles.

action: Grab (Radius 266-416 px, Strength 0.400) reshapes the forearm and upper arm to match the reference, then pulls the buttock out from the side.
view: close perspective, arm; then side of hip
why: Match reference; enlarge buttocks with a large Grab from the side.

action: Crease Polish (Radius 338 px) idle in Sculpt Mode; selects arms plus shoulder piece in Object Mode, Ctrl+J, then Ctrl+R; a blue Face Set colour patch appears on the arm from a stray key.
why: Join arms with shoulders; a stray Face Set patch needs clearing.

action: Clay Strips (Radius 120-424 px, Strength 0.500) runs from shoulder down onto the arm with Shift smoothing so the shoulder overlaps the arm.
why: Shoulder overlaps the arm like a chain link.

action: Crease Polish (Radius 64-88 px, Strength 0.250) draws the central back line; one stroke undone with Ctrl+Z; view orbits behind the figure.
why: Back separation line.

action: Ctrl+Tab out of Sculpt Mode, Alt+H, zooms out to the whole stiff A-pose figure with the concept docked left.
why: Judge the full silhouette.

action: Annotate pen circles the head in front and side views; narrator concludes head and feet look too small and will be scaled up.
view: right then front perspective, whole figure
why: Proportion pass against the concept.
reader_equivalent: ob.scale scaled about the neck/ankle pivot, then outline_match
